# FAQ-006 Engineering FAQ #6

Revision: Rev A

Related documents: MM-P2-L1-SB03, SB-1031, SB-1046

Q: What is the recommended way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01), and why is it set that way?
A: The way lube refill interval for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 40 hours. Background: the interval is set to maintain consistent film thickness on the guideways and ball screws under the machine's duty cycle and contamination risk in the heat treat cell. Rationale: frequent top-up prevents dry starts and reduces abrasive wear from furnace-borne particulates. Practical example: if the machine is run in a high-cycle production pattern that exposes it to frequent thermal cycling and dust, follow the stated interval exactly and avoid extending it. Records to keep: log each refill with date, time, technician initials, lube product batch, and pre- and post-refill way readings where applicable. Reference inspection notes to MM-P2-L1-SB03 for the lube material specification and acceptable contamination limits.

Q: How often should shot media be topped up for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02), and what indicators should trigger an immediate top-up?
A: The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 45 hours. Background: media attrition and carryout in a hot forging environment reduces media size distribution and effective cleaning energy over time. Rationale: maintaining target media volume and size distribution preserves blast coverage and prevents accelerated wear of cabinet components. Indicators for immediate top-up: visible reduction in blast performance, increased cycle time to achieve specified cleanliness, or elevated media fines reported during sampling. Practical example: when a process audit shows escalating rework rates tied to surface cleanliness, perform a top-up and record pre- and post-top-up blast performance metrics. Records to keep: media top-up log entry with equipment id, media type, supplier lot number, operator initials, and inspection comments. See SB-1031 for media handling and disposal guidance.

Q: What is the specified blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01), and why must it be followed exactly?
A: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 100 N·m. Background: proper liner bolt torque ensures even clamping of liners, preventing vibration, liner movement, and accelerated wear of wheel components. Rationale: under-torqued bolts allow relative motion that leads to fretting and fatigue; over-torqued bolts can distort liners and compromise bolt integrity. Practical example: during liner replacement, torque bolts to the specified value using a calibrated torque wrench; sequence the torque steps evenly across the liner circumference to achieve uniform seating. Records to keep: maintenance report listing equipment id, torque tool serial number, calibration date, technician initials, liner part id, and bolt torque confirmation for each bolt position. Cross-reference SB-1046 for wheel assembly replacement procedures.

Q: What torque should be applied to the blast wheel liner bolts for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03), and what special precautions apply?
A: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 50 N·m. Background: this cabinet uses a different liner material and bolt specification that requires a lower clamping torque to prevent thread stripping and to account for thermal expansion in the Hot Forge environment. Rationale: using the specified torque prevents both mechanical failure and distortion while maintaining acceptable sealing between liner sections. Practical example: before torquing, clean bolt threads and apply the manufacturer-specified anti-seize per MM-P2-L1-SB03; then torque each bolt to the specified value and record the result. Records to keep: bolt torque checklist including equipment id, bolt positions, torque achieved, tool calibration id, technician initials, and any deviations or corrective actions taken.

Q: What is the correct main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03), and what documentation should accompany the torque operation?
A: The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 1575 N·m. Background: the main ram bolts are primary load carriers; correct torque is critical to maintain clamping preload and prevent joint loosening under forging loads. Rationale: insufficient preload can lead to fatigue failure of the bolts and loss of positional accuracy; correct torque ensures joint integrity while allowing for predictable tension under load. Practical example: perform torque application with a calibrated hydraulic torque wrench rated for the specified value; use the manufacturer-recommended tightening sequence and re-check after initial warm-up cycles as specified in the press maintenance schedule. Records to keep: torque application report containing equipment id, bolt identifiers, final torque readings, torque tool serial number and calibration certificate reference, technician initials, and any re-tightening actions. See SB-1046 for bolting safety procedures and MM-P2-L1-SB03 for approved lubricants and anti-seize compounds to use on threads prior to torqueing.

End of FAQ.
